label: Symplectic Group Actions and Moment Maps
notes: This chapter, spanning printed pages 191 through 251, turns symmetry into geometry. A Lie group acting by symplectomorphisms produces conserved quantities, packaged in a single moment map. We will see how that one object generates examples, quotients, convex polytopes, and a dictionary linking symplectic geometry to representation theory and algebraic invariants.

label: Symplectic and Hamiltonian Actions
notes: An action is symplectic when every group element preserves the form, and Hamiltonian when each infinitesimal generator is a globally Hamiltonian vector field. The gap between these notions is measured by cohomology classes, and only Hamiltonian actions admit the moment map machinery developed across the rest of the chapter.

label: The Moment Map
notes: The moment map sends the manifold into the dual of the Lie algebra so that pairing it with any generator yields that generator's Hamiltonian function. The defining identity packages every component Hamiltonian at once, and its differential recovers the contraction of the fundamental vector field with omega.

label: Equivariance and Conservation
notes: A moment map is equivariant when it intertwines the group action with the coadjoint action on the dual algebra. Equivariance makes the level sets group-invariant, so the moment map components Poisson-commute exactly when the group is abelian, giving the conserved quantities driving Noether's theorem.

label: Example: The Circle on the Sphere
notes: Rotation of the two-sphere about its vertical axis preserves the area form, and its moment map is simply the height function. The poles are the fixed points, the regular level sets are latitude circles, and the moment image is the closed height interval between the two poles.

label: Linear and Torus Actions
notes: For the standard torus acting on complex space by phase rotations, the moment map records half the squared modulus in each coordinate. Its image is the positive orthant, and on projective space the constraint of fixed total radius cuts this orthant down to a bounded simplex.

label: Symplectic Reduction
notes: Marsden and Weinstein showed that the zero level set of an equivariant moment map, divided by the group, is again a symplectic manifold. When zero is a regular value and the action is free, the reduced space inherits a unique form pulling back to the restriction of omega on the level set.

label: The Reduced Symplectic Form
notes: On the quotient the reduced form is characterized by the condition that its pullback along the quotient projection equals the pullback of omega to the level set. Dimension drops by twice the group dimension, since one direction is killed by the constraint and one by the group orbit.

label: Atiyah-Guillemin-Sternberg Convexity
notes: For a torus acting on a compact connected symplectic manifold, the image of the moment map is a convex polytope. Its vertices are the images of the fixed points, and each fibre over an interior point is connected, a striking rigidity hidden inside the smooth dynamics.

label: The Moment Polytope
notes: The moment polytope is the convex hull of the fixed-point images. Complex projective plane gives a triangle whose three vertices are the coordinate fixed points, while the product of two spheres gives a square. The polytope encodes the manifold's toric combinatorics in a single picture.

label: Delzant's Theorem and Toric Manifolds
notes: Delzant classified compact toric symplectic manifolds by their polytopes. A polytope is admissible when it is simple, rational, and smooth at every vertex, and each such Delzant polytope reconstructs a unique toric manifold together with its torus action and moment map.

label: Links to Geometric Invariant Theory
notes: The Kempf-Ness theorem identifies the symplectic quotient with the geometric invariant theory quotient of the complexified group. Vanishing of the moment map selects, within each closed complex orbit, the points of minimal norm, matching polystable orbits and tying reduction to stability in algebraic geometry.

label: Recap and Outlook
notes: Symmetry produced a moment map, the moment map produced quotients and convex polytopes, and those polytopes classified toric manifolds and connected to invariant theory. Carry forward the picture of height on the sphere and the triangle of projective space as the canonical images of this entire circle of ideas.
